The DCA flight gives about 36 minutes from landing to registration opening; the 9:05 IAD flight lands only 2 hours 26 minutes before registration closes, before accounting for the longer transfer.

A realistic hotel arrival is 5:15-5:35 p.m., leaving 1 hour 55 minutes to 2 hours 15 minutes before registration closes. A taxi or rideshare is estimated at 20-35 minutes and $24-$38, with a hotel arrival around 5:05-5:25 p.m. Through IAD at 5:04 p.m., allow 20-30 minutes to exit, about 55-65 minutes on the Silver Line plus the transfer and walk, and arrival around 6:35-6:55 p.m. A rideshare is estimated at 45-75 minutes and $68-$95, putting arrival around 6:10-6:50 p.m. Traffic could erase most of that margin.
user: Then the later Dulles flight is not a serious option. Compare the 7:20 Dulles flight against DCA, and check Friday returns that work after 3:15 without leaving the meeting early.
assistant: The 7:20 a.m. IAD flight lands at 3:18 p.m. Metro would put you at the hotel around 4:50-5:10 p.m.; rideshare around 4:25-5:05 p.m. That is workable for registration. Friday nonstop returns are DCA-SFO at 5:35-8:52 p.m. for the $586 itinerary and IAD-SFO at 6:10-9:29 p.m. for the $527 itinerary. There is also an IAD departure at 7:45-11:04 p.m. for $552 round trip.
user: Can I make the 5:35 from Reagan after a 3:15 finish? Assume I need to retrieve my bag from the hotel, although I will not be checking it at the airport.
assistant: It is possible but compressed. If the session releases at 3:15, allow 10 minutes to exit, 10-15 minutes to walk to the hotel and collect the bag, then 20-35 minutes by taxi to DCA. Estimated terminal arrival is 4:05-4:25 p.m., or 70-90 minutes before departure. Metro would more likely produce a 4:20-4:40 arrival. The taxi plan has a usable margin, but a late session or heavy traffic would reduce it quickly.
user: What about the IAD returns? I do not want a comparison that assumes Friday traffic will be favorable.
assistant: For the 6:10 p.m. IAD flight, leaving the hotel around 3:40 after collecting the bag gives 2 hours 30 minutes to departure. The Silver Line trip, including the transfer and airport walk, is approximately 70-85 minutes, for terminal arrival around 4:50-5:05. That leaves 65-80 minutes and little recovery time for a delayed session. The 7:45 p.m. flight is much stronger: the same transit plan leaves about 2 hours 40 minutes after arrival at IAD. A Friday rideshare may take 60-100 minutes and cost about $75-$110, so Metro is more predictable even though it is slower on paper.
user: Now check the block. I need the tax-inclusive amount, cancellation deadline, destination fee, and whether storing the bag Friday creates another charge.
assistant: The conference block is $289 per night for March 2-5. With 15.95% lodging tax, the three-night total is $1,005.18. The usual $32 nightly destination fee is waived for reservations made through the block. Wi-Fi and fitness-center access are included. The reservation can be canceled without penalty until 6:00 p.m. local time on Friday, February 26; after that, the penalty is one night plus tax, $335.10. The hotel will hold a registered guest's bag on departure day at no charge, though gratuity is discretionary. The block currently closes February 5 or when its inventory sells out.
user: Is there a materially less expensive hotel nearby that does not introduce a difficult Wednesday morning? Compare one, but include every mandatory fee.
assistant: A business hotel four blocks north is $244 nightly. Its mandatory $25 nightly facility fee and 15.95% tax bring three nights to $935.73, only $69.45 below the block. It is about a 10-minute walk from the conference hotel, so Wednesday remains manageable if you leave around 8:30 for an 8:45 room check. Its cancellation deadline is 48 hours before arrival, and bag storage is complimentary. The savings are modest relative to having registration, the presentation room, and Friday bag retrieval in the same building.
user: Keep the conference block in the primary combinations. Calculate the complete totals using Metro where it is practical, but use a taxi from Reagan on Tuesday because that arrival margin matters. Include airport transfers in both directions.
assistant: Combination A is DCA both ways: $586 airfare, $1,005.18 hotel, Tuesday taxi estimated at $31, and Friday taxi estimated at $31, for a planning total of $1,653.18. It reaches the hotel around 5:05-5:25 p.m. Tuesday. Friday terminal arrival is estimated at 4:05-4:25 for the 5:35 flight. Combination B is IAD both ways using the early Tuesday flight and 7:45 p.m. Friday return: $552 airfare, $1,005.18 hotel, and approximately $13.50 total for four Metro rides involved in the two airport journeys, for $1,570.68. It reaches the hotel around 4:50-5:10 Tuesday and allows a much wider Friday departure margin.
user: Why are there four Metro rides? That wording is confusing. Also show the IAD option with the 6:10 return so I can see what the lower fare actually buys.
assistant: The IAD estimate covers two airport trips, each requiring a Silver Line ride and a short connecting Metro ride, hence four individual fares. The combined estimated cost is still $13.50. With the 6:10 p.m. return, the round-trip airfare is $527 and the total becomes $1,545.68. That saves $25 versus the 7:45 return, but the expected airport arrival is only 65-80 minutes before departure. The savings do not compensate for the tighter Friday margin.
user: Agreed. Give me the two approval choices, with the operational tradeoff stated plainly. Do not book anything yet.
assistant: Approval choice 1: DCA convenience option, $1,653.18 projected total. Fly SFO-DCA Tuesday 8:10 a.m.-4:24 p.m., take a taxi to the conference hotel, stay three nights in the $1,005.18 block, and fly DCA-SFO Friday 5:35-8:52 p.m. This has the shortest Tuesday transfer and the simplest airport access, but Friday is tight: estimated terminal arrival is 70-90 minutes before departure if the meeting ends on time.

Approval choice 2: IAD margin option, $1,570.68 projected total. Fly SFO-IAD Tuesday 7:20 a.m.-3:18 p.m., use Metro to reach the hotel around 4:50-5:10 p.m., stay in the same block, and fly IAD-SFO Friday 7:45-11:04 p.m. Metro should reach IAD around 4:50-5:05 p.m., leaving roughly 2 hours 40 minutes before departure. It costs $82.50 less and provides the stronger Friday margin, at the expense of an earlier Tuesday departure and longer transfers.

Both choices preserve Tuesday registration time and the full Friday program. The block is refundable through 6:00 p.m. Eastern on February 26 and has not been reserved. Choice 2 is the more resilient overall itinerary; Choice 1 is reasonable if minimizing ground-transfer time is more important than Friday schedule cushion.
